tasks.instruction: The function should return true exactly when every bit set in the second argument is also set in the first argument.
tasks.note: Start returns the negation; the wrong edit compares the masked value with the first argument (the reverse containment).

tasks.instruction: Return true when the three lengths form a non-degenerate triangle: each pair of sides must sum to strictly more than the third side.
tasks.note: Lengths kept small so no addition wraps; a degenerate case on each side.

tasks.instruction: Return true when at least two of the three flags are true.
tasks.note: Start uses exclusive or for the final combine, wrong when all three are true.

tasks.instruction: The function should add up p0+i for every i from 0 through 6 inclusive (seven terms), with wrapping addition.
The function returns the position of the largest element; when the largest value occurs more than once it must return the earliest such position.
Besides writing the value at the given position, also write it at the next position (wrapping from the last position back to the first).
tasks.note: Positions are taken modulo 4, which handles the wrap.

tasks.instruction: The function should count the positions at which the two arrays hold equal values.
tasks.note: The last slot matters for the fold count.

tasks.instruction: Keep only the lowest p1 bits of p0; when p1 is 32 or more the whole value must be kept.
tasks.note: Shift distance wraps at 32, so the start yields 0 for 32 and wrong masks above.

tasks.instruction: Return the wrapped product and a flag that is true only when the true product does not fit in 32 bits; a zero first factor must never report overflow.
tasks.note: Division by zero gives all ones, which wrongly flagged zero factors.

tasks.instruction: The timer now runs at 1024 ticks per second instead of 1000; convert a tick count to whole milliseconds (multiply first, with wrapping, then round down).
tasks.note: The product wraps for large tick counts, matching the stated arithmetic.

tasks.instruction: The function should read the array as four base-2 digits with the first element most significant, returning 8*a0 + 4*a1 + 2*a2 + a3 (wrapping).
tasks.note: The helper is one Horner step.

tasks.instruction: Apply the hailstone step five times: halve an even value, otherwise replace it with three times the value plus one (wrapping).
Return true when any two neighbouring elements of the array add up (with wrapping) to the target.
tasks.note: Each neighbour pair is the only match in some test.

tasks.instruction: Compare the two values as two's-complement signed numbers: return true when the first is less than the second.
tasks.note: Flipping the sign bit of both operands maps signed order onto unsigned order.

tasks.instruction: Return the four-bit field of p0 that starts at bit position p1 (bits p1 to p1+3), using only the low five bits of p1.
tasks.note: Shift distance uses the low five bits.

tasks.instruction: Return the value with its top bit cleared, together with a flag telling whether the top bit was set.
